stages.title: THE CENTRAL QUESTION OF THE CLAUSE AND THE THREE DOORS FROM WRONG TO PUNISHMENT

pills.text: WRONG, CRIME, PUNISHMENT ARE THREE DOORS
OVERLAP IS THE PARADIGM, NOT THE WHOLE
ABHORRENCE IS NOT A LICENCE TO PUNISH

sequence: Ask when a wrong may be turned into a crime
Separate wrongdoing, criminalisation and punishment
Place the overlap of legal crime and moral wrong
Run harm, rights, public wrong, culpability, proportionality
Only then open the question of punishment

groups.heading: THE QUESTION THE CLAUSE ACTUALLY ASKS
items: When, and on what terms, may a political community turn a wrong into a crime and attach punishment to it?
Wrongdoing, criminalisation and punishment are three separate steps with three separate justifications.
Abhorrence at the conduct licenses none of the three by itself.

groups.heading: CRIME AND MORAL WRONG: THE THREE REGIONS
items: Law only: an unjust statute criminalises morally innocent conduct.
Overlap: murder and theft are legal and moral wrongs at once, and this is the paradigm.
Wrong only: a grave moral wrong the criminal code has never reached.

groups.heading: THE FIVE-GATE CRIMINALISATION FILTER
items: Harm, rights, public wrong, culpability and proportionality operate in series, not as a checklist.
Failing any single gate defeats criminalisation however strongly the conduct is disliked.
Clearing all five leaves the justification of punishment entirely untouched.

stages.mechanism_strip: Positive law fixes the rule, the moral account tests its justice and the sociological account exposes its bias, so criminalisation must clear five gates of its own.
stages.answer_line: Wrongdoing, criminalisation and punishment are three doors with three different keys, and the standard failure is to open the third by pointing at the room behind the first.

stages.title: CONDITIONS OF RESPONSIBLE PUNISHMENT AND THE CLASSIFICATION OF THE FIVE THEORIES

pills.text: CULPABILITY IS GRADED, NOT A SWITCH
CONDITIONS CONSTRAIN, THEY DO NOT CHOOSE

sequence: Define punishment as hard treatment plus censure
Check the seven enabling conditions in order
Grade culpability rather than switching it on
Separate responsibility from causal contribution
Choose among five theories by test and danger

groups.heading: WHAT PUNISHMENT IS, PRECISELY
items: Hard treatment together with authoritative censure, imposed by a competent public authority for a proved breach.
Public, proportionate, impartial and rule-governed, which is exactly what private vengeance is not.

groups.heading: SEVEN CONDITIONS OF RESPONSIBLE PUNISHMENT
items: Law known in advance, voluntary act or relevant omission, culpability graded by intention, knowledge, recklessness and negligence.
Fair procedure and reliable proof, a competent and impartial authority, proportionality, and equal application without status bias.
Responsibility is not causal contribution: one may contribute without knowledge or control, and an official may be responsible for culpable omission.

groups.heading: FIVE THEORIES BY TEST AND BY DANGER
items: Retributive desert and deterrent prevention are the two poles; incapacitation adds necessity and risk.
Reformative reintegration and restorative repair complete the field.
Each theory carries its own danger: vengeance, instrumentalisation, indefinite custody, paternalism and unequal bargaining.

stages.mechanism_strip: Legality, voluntariness, graded culpability, reliable proof, impartiality, proportionality and equal application constrain every candidate theory without choosing among them.
stages.answer_line: Punishment is not revenge with paperwork: public, proportionate and impartial hard treatment on a responsible agent under rules known in advance is a different institution altogether.

stages.title: THE RETRIBUTIVE ARGUMENT: DESERT AS GROUND AND AS CEILING

pills.text: HEGEL: ANNULMENT OF THE WRONGFUL CLAIM

sequence: The crime asserts a maxim against equal right
Imputable agency makes the offender answerable
Proportionate response publicly denies the maxim
Denial expresses respect for right, not revenge
Limiting retributivism caps rather than demands

groups.heading: THE FOUR-STEP RETRIBUTIVE ARGUMENT
items: The crime asserts a maxim incompatible with equal right, and imputable agency makes the offender answerable for it.
A proportionate legal response publicly denies that maxim rather than repaying the injury.
The denial therefore expresses respect for right and for the offender's standing as a responsible agent.

groups.heading: KANT AND HEGEL, DOING DIFFERENT WORK
items: Kant: punishment answers the culpable act, and the offender is an end who may not be used merely as an instrument of deterrence.
Hegel: punishment is the annulment of the crime's wrongful claim, restoring right while taking the offender seriously.

groups.heading: THE RIGHTS OBJECTION AND THE LIMITING REPLY
items: Objection: suffering does not undo suffering, so desert alone cannot show why the state should add pain.
Reply: limiting retributivism forbids punishment without desert and beyond desert rather than demanding it.
Residual limit: the limiting form supplies no positive general justifying aim of its own.

stages.mechanism_strip: An imputable act asserts a maxim against equal right, and a proportionate public denial of that maxim is what distinguishes penal justice from private retaliation.
stages.answer_line: Retribution is not vengeance made respectable: the offender's own act, and not the community's appetite for suffering, fixes both the ground and the ceiling of the sanction.

stages.title: DETERRENCE AND INCAPACITATION WEIGHED ON THE SAME AXES
sequence: Split prevention into reasons and opportunities
State the four presuppositions of the threat
Certainty and promptness outrank severity
Locate the objection at liability and at amount
Flag the deterrent effect as contested
matrix: the offender's practical reasoning about cost
the offender's opportunity to act at all
a known, certain and prompt credible threat
expected prevention net of collateral harm
necessity and a defensible judgment of risk
liability: it permits punishing a known innocent
the comparative effect is empirically contested
secure imprisonment already achieves the same end

groups.heading: TWO ARGUMENTS, TWO TARGETS
items: Deterrence operates on the offender's practical reasoning about perceived costs.
Incapacitation operates on opportunity and bypasses the offender's reasons altogether.

groups.heading: PRESUPPOSITIONS THAT MUST BE STATED
items: Persons respond to perceived costs, and sanctions are known and sufficiently certain.
Preventive benefit exceeds direct and collateral harm, and less harmful alternatives are inadequate.
Certainty and promptness of sanction outrank severity as levers of prevention.

groups.heading: WHERE THE CLASSIC OBJECTION LANDS
items: Pure deterrence permits convicting a known innocent where the preventive yield is high enough.
Rule-utilitarian legality and due process reply; the rejoinder is that protection then rests on a calculation.
Comparative deterrent effect is an empirical controversy and must never be reported as settled.

stages.mechanism_strip: Prevention through credible threat and prevention through restraint rest on different presuppositions, so each has to carry its own justification in an answer.
stages.answer_line: Deterrence works on the offender's reasons and incapacitation works on his opportunities, so an argument that succeeds for one has not yet succeeded for the other.

stages.title: REFORM, DIGNITY AND THE TWO PROPORTIONALITY DIMENSIONS FOR JUVENILES

pills.text: NATURE OF THE CRIME IS NOT CONCLUSIVE

sequence: Persons are more than their worst act
Agency can be impaired and rebuilt
Use capability rather than degradation
Rank ordinally, then fix the cardinal anchor
Integrate offence-centred and offender-centred views

groups.heading: THE DIGNITY ARGUMENT IN FOUR STEPS
items: Persons are more than their worst act, and responsible agency can be impaired and rebuilt.
A humane state reduces future wrongdoing through restored capability rather than degradation.
Punishment must therefore preserve a route back into membership.

groups.heading: TWO DIMENSIONS OF PROPORTIONALITY
items: Ordinal proportionality ranks offences against one another.
Cardinal proportionality fixes how severe the whole penal scale may be.
The juvenile case turns on the cardinal anchor once reduced agency lowers culpability.

groups.heading: JUVENILES AND THE BOUNDING CONDITIONS
items: Seriousness of harm, intention and understanding, developmental capacity, susceptibility to influence, prospects of reform and procedural reliability.
The nature of the crime is relevant but not conclusive, and the two perspectives are integrated rather than ranked.
Rehabilitation stays bounded by the proportionate band, consent where possible, periodic review and rights.

stages.mechanism_strip: Ordinal ranking fixes relative seriousness while the cardinal anchor fixes the scale, and reduced juvenile agency lowers the deserved point on that scale.
stages.answer_line: Reform is not leniency: it accepts responsibility and proportionate restraint, and adds only that a state which closes the route back has punished the person rather than the offence.

stages.title: THE THREE-QUESTION GRID AND THE MIXED OR LIMITING THEORY

pills.text: PREVENTION IN AIM, DESERT IN CONSTRAINT
ONE ANSWER TO THREE QUESTIONS FAILS

sequence: Ask why the institution should exist at all
Ask whom we may punish and on what condition
Ask how much punishment is permissible
Assign prevention to aim and desert to constraint
Give each classic objection its own address
matrix: why should the institution exist at all?
forward-looking prevention, protection and restored security
whom may we punish, and on what condition?
desert: proved guilt, a voluntary act, graded culpability
proportionality: ordinal ranking and a cardinal ceiling
how do the three answers fit together?
a mixed theory, consequentialist in aim and retributivist in constraint
any theory giving one answer to all three

groups.heading: THREE QUESTIONS THAT MUST BE SEPARATED
items: Q1 asks why the institution of punishment should exist at all.
Q2 asks whom we may punish and on what condition.
Q3 asks how much punishment is permissible.

groups.heading: THE SEPARATION ARGUMENT
items: An institution may be justified by its general benefit while its applications follow an independent principle of fairness.
The point of a promise-keeping practice differs from the rules deciding who is bound by a particular promise.
Prevention therefore supplies the aim while desert supplies the side-constraint.

groups.heading: WHAT THE GRID BUYS THE ANSWER
items: Punishing the innocent is an objection to deterrence at Q2, not at Q1.
Why the state must inflict suffering is an objection to retributivism at Q1, not at Q2 or Q3.
The presupposition that aim and application can come apart is exactly what a pure retributivist denies.

stages.mechanism_strip: An institution may be justified by its general benefit while its application follows an independent principle of fairness, which is ordinary institutional reasoning rather than an evasion.
stages.answer_line: Retribution and deterrence stop being rivals once one notices that prevention explains why the institution exists while desert explains whom it may touch and how far.

stages.title: EXPRESSIVE, COMMUNICATIVE AND RESTORATIVE THEORIES COMPARED
sequence: Distinguish punishment from a mere penalty
Convert expression into an address to the offender
Test the polity's standing to call to account
Ask who was hurt and what repair requires
Keep the disciplinary reading in the critical paragraph
matrix: a two-way address to the offender
relational among victim, offender and community
the object of an authoritative judgment
a rational participant capable of answering
an active participant expected to repair
the vehicle that makes censure credible
a secular penance focusing attention on the wrong
measured by what repair actually requires
has this polity the standing to demand penance?
is participation voluntary, safe and undominated?

groups.heading: WHAT MAKES PUNISHMENT MORE THAN A PENALTY
items: A parking fine and a conviction both impose hardship; only the second carries authoritative reprobation.
This explains why wrongful conviction is a distinct wrong, why degrading punishment is objectionable apart from severity, and why acquittal is a vindication.

groups.heading: FROM EXPRESSION TO ADDRESS TO REPAIR
items: Duff converts one-way expression into a two-way address, with hard treatment as secular penance.
The standing condition makes penal legitimacy conditional on the justice of the order that punishes.
Restorative process asks who was hurt, what they need and whose obligation it is to repair.

groups.heading: MECHANISM, LIMIT AND THE CRITICAL CAVEAT
items: Reintegrative shaming condemns the act and keeps the route back; stigmatising shaming condemns the person and is criminogenic.
Restorative process is conditionally appropriate: voluntariness, prior safety and no entrenched domination.
Foucault supplies a genealogy of penal power and never a normative justification, and names no technology or state.

stages.mechanism_strip: Hard treatment makes condemnation credible, the same burden addressed to a citizen becomes secular penance, and reintegrative disapproval preserves the bonds that give censure force.
stages.answer_line: Condemnation supplies the meaning of punishment, communication its address to the offender and restoration the repair of harm, which is why retribution against reform is a false alternative.

stages.title: CORRUPTION: ENTRUSTED POWER, PARTICULARISM AND THE SYSTEMIC-ETHICAL VERDICT

pills.text: PARTICULAR LOYALTY INSIDE A UNIVERSAL ROLE
TRUST, IMPARTIALITY, RULE OF LAW, AGENCY
AN ETHICAL ACT IN A SYSTEMIC ECOLOGY

sequence: Name the entrusted power that was misused
Trace trust, impartiality, law and civic agency
Set particular loyalty against the universal role
Diagnose character and structure together
Close on the ethical act in a systemic ecology

groups.heading: WHY CORRUPTION IS A DISTINCTIVE WRONG
items: Misuse of entrusted public or institutional power through partial, concealed or improperly exchanged advantage.
Wider than bribery: favouritism, nepotism, embezzlement, regulatory capture and abuse of discretion.
It breaches fiduciary trust, violates impartiality, injures the rule of law and reduces citizens to supplicants.

groups.heading: PARTICULARISM INSIDE A UNIVERSALIST ROLE
items: Personal relations generate genuine duties, and public office is entrusted for a specified common purpose.
Corruption occurs when a legitimate particular loyalty is acted upon inside a role governed by universal criteria.
The remedy is role boundaries, conflict-of-interest rules and recusal, not the abolition of loyalty.

groups.heading: THE SYSTEMIC-ETHICAL VERDICT
items: Ethical diagnosis targets character; systemic diagnosis targets opacity, monopoly, discretion and impunity.
The defensible position is that corruption is an ethical act inside a systemic ecology.
No regime type is automatically immune, and the enacted Indian frameworks settle no ethical question.

stages.mechanism_strip: Office creates fiduciary obligations, so acting on a legitimate particular loyalty inside a universalist role converts loyalty itself into the wrong of corruption.
stages.answer_line: Corruption is distinctive not because of what it costs but because power held in trust was turned to partial use inside a role that was created to be impartial.

stages.title: MASS VIOLENCE: MECHANISMS AND THE FIVE KINDS OF COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY
sequence: Organisation multiplies ordinary agency
Dehumanisation withdraws ordinary restraints
Bureaucracy routinises harm as role-performance
Differentiate responsibility across the roles
Keep guilt individual and refuse inherited guilt

groups.heading: MECHANISMS THAT LOWER THE THRESHOLD
items: Dehumanisation, moral exclusion and diffusion of responsibility withdraw ordinary restraints from an out-group.
Obedience, bureaucracy, polarisation, propaganda and the security dilemma routinise participation.
Arendt's thesis about thoughtlessness concerns the psychology of perpetration, never the degree of guilt.

groups.heading: FIVE KINDS OF COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY
items: Criminal guilt attaches to individuals; organisational liability attaches to bodies with real decision procedures.
Political responsibility grounds duties of reparation, memory and reform for citizens collectively.
Responsibility for omission is graded by knowledge and capacity; inherited or metaphysical guilt is rejected outright.

groups.heading: RELIGIOUSLY FRAMED VIOLENCE: THREE SEPARATIONS
items: A tradition's texts and a movement's political use of them are not the same object.
Communal violence, pogrom and genocide differ in structure and evidentiary requirement, not merely in scale.
Victims may be selected by religious identity for instrumental political reasons, so the marker is not the motive.

stages.mechanism_strip: Dehumanisation, moral exclusion, diffusion of responsibility and bureaucratic routine lower the threshold at which ordinary agents participate in organised harm.
stages.answer_line: Mass violence is distinctive because organisation multiplies ordinary agency, which is why guilt must stay individual while responsibility is differentiated across every role.

stages.title: GENOCIDE: LEMKIN'S COINAGE, THE 1948 CONVENTION AND THE NEIGHBOURING CATEGORIES

pills.text: DESTRUCTION OF A GROUP AS SUCH
A FORM OF SHARED LIFE IS DESTROYED

sequence: Lemkin coins the term in 1944
The Convention is adopted in 1948
It enters into force in 1951
Specific intent against four protected categories
Distinguish it from the neighbouring categories

groups.heading: HOW THE CONCEPT WAS CONSTRUCTED
items: Lemkin coined genocide in Axis Rule in Occupied Europe in 1944, from Greek genos and Latin -cide.
He conceived it as a coordinated plan aimed at destroying the essential foundations of the life of a group.
The 1948 Convention entered into force in 1951 and requires specific intent against four protected categories.

groups.heading: WHY THE EXTRA CATEGORY IS NEEDED
items: Victims are attacked as members of a group marked for destruction, and generational continuity is targeted.
The additional wrong is the destruction of a form of shared life, which counting murders does not capture.
The perpetrator claims the power to decide which human plurality may continue to exist.

groups.heading: PRECISION THE EXAMINER REWARDS
items: The adopted text is narrower than Lemkin's conception, and political groups are not protected categories.
Genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and generic mass violence are four distinct categories.
Specific intent may be inferred from a pattern of conduct, but moral outrage cannot substitute for evidence.

stages.mechanism_strip: Where the aim becomes the destruction of a group's shared life rather than the harming of its members, the wrong changes in kind rather than merely in degree.
stages.answer_line: Genocide is not a very large massacre: what makes it a distinct wrong is that the continued existence of a group, and the shared life that sustains it, was itself the target.

stages.title: CAPITAL PUNISHMENT: THE ARGUMENT TREE, OBJECTIONS AND REPLIES

pills.text: IRREVERSIBLE, AND IT REMOVES THE AGENT

sequence: State what makes the case philosophically hard
Build the argument tree on both sides
Concede that rights admit limits in defence
Apply the custody and necessity distinction
Classify each Indian illustration precisely

groups.heading: THE ARGUMENT TREE, BOTH SIDES AT FULL STRENGTH
items: For: desert for the gravest culpable killing, incapacitation, and public affirmation of the equal value of victims.
Against: fallibility and irreversibility, dignity, unequal administration, and the foreclosure of reform.
The deterrence branch is empirically contested on both sides and must be flagged rather than asserted.

groups.heading: THE CUSTODY DISTINCTION
items: A right may be fundamental without being exceptionless, and it yields to a present unjust threat.
Execution follows custody and adjudication, when less final means of incapacitation are already available.
The defensive permission therefore does not transfer, and the abolitionist case runs through necessity.

groups.heading: THE INDIAN ILLUSTRATIONS, CORRECTLY CLASSIFIED
items: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) is a Supreme Court judgment that retained the penalty with the rarest of rare limitation.
Law Commission of India Report No. 262 (2015) is an advisory report recommending abolition for ordinary crimes, excluding specified terrorism-related and war contexts.
Each is a dated legal fact and never a philosophical proof.

stages.mechanism_strip: Immediate defence answers a present unjust threat while execution follows custody and adjudication, so the defensive permission does not transfer to the custodial case.
stages.answer_line: The decisive move on any death-penalty stem is the custody distinction: a right that yields to an ongoing unjust threat has not yielded to a calm decision about a restrained person.

stages.title: INTEGRATED ANSWER SPINE, DIRECTIVE DECODER AND THE GRADED VERDICT BANK

pills.text: A SURVEY IS NOT AN ANSWER

sequence: Decode the directive before the topic
Name the penal question actually at issue
Adjudicate one live rival, not four
Classify the illustration correctly
Close with a conditional graded verdict

groups.heading: FOUR STANDING DEBATES
items: Kant against Bentham: desert against prevention, backward against forward, sanctified suffering against instrumentalised persons.
Retribution against reform is a false alternative once desert sets the upper limit and reform works inside it.
Arendt against monster theories, and particular loyalty against public impartiality, complete the field.

groups.heading: THE DIRECTIVE DECIDES THE STRUCTURE
items: Explain gives internal logic; discuss adds one adjudicated tension; critically examine makes objection and reply the answer.
Is X justified separates the three questions; is X a form of Y states Y's conditions before applying them.
Do you agree demands a qualified commitment at the outset rather than a survey.

groups.heading: THE UNIVERSAL SPINE AND THE GRADED VERDICT
items: Name the penal question, separate Q1, Q2 and Q3, state the strongest rival, work one objection with its reply and residual limit.
Add one correctly classified illustration and close with a graded verdict that names its conditions.
Separate philosophical validity from implementation and from empirical effect: that separation is the marked move.

stages.mechanism_strip: Identifying which penal question is being asked converts a shapeless survey into an adjudication, and the graded verdict then states the conditions under which it holds.
stages.answer_line: Marks in this clause are carried not by the catalogue of theories but by separating the justifying question, adjudicating one live rival and stating the conditions of the verdict.

stages.title: SUBORDINATE ENRICHMENT — ONLY AFTER THE COMPLETE CORE

pills.text: COMMUNICATIVE AND RESTORATIVE ARE ALREADY CORE
DOES RESTORATION SCALE TO MASS CRIME?

groups.heading: WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPTIONAL
items: Whether censure-communication can be coercively delivered without collapsing into hard treatment justified on other grounds.
Whether restorative practice scales to grave and mass crimes, and how it interacts with victim inequality.
Abolition against tightly constrained retention of the death penalty, once the Core moral justifications and rights objections are already secure.

groups.heading: THE ADVANCED OBJECTION AND ITS REPLY
items: Restorative or communicative models can underplay the moral seriousness of grave wrongs and fail victims who need public denunciation.
The best restorative view is not anti-censure: it preserves condemnation while refusing vengeance as the sole mode of justice.
It is strongest exactly where reintegration and differentiated responsibility matter most.

groups.heading: WHAT IS ALREADY CORE, AND WHAT NOT TO OVER-STUDY
items: Communicative punishment and restorative justice were promoted into the Core, so only their residual questions belong here.
Collective and command responsibility sharpens the genocide and mass-violence analysis beyond the minimum, and is the next promotion candidate.
Do not collect crime statistics, prison data or convention lists, and do not turn genocide into a historical catalogue: keep theory first.

stages.mechanism_strip: This optional depth is unnecessary for a competent core answer; use it only for added nuance after the complete core has been written.
